newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures higher on weak yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures higher on weak yen.

text.p: Tokyo gold futures ended firmer across the board on Wednesday, as the yen's weakness against the dollar, triggered by a weaker-than-expected tankan survey announced by the Bank of Japan, boosted the market, traders said. Activity remained lacklustre. The newly listed benchmark August ended at 1,343 yen on Wednesday after opening at 1,340 yen on Wednesday.

Other contracts ranged from three to 11 yen per gram higher. "From the afternoon session, gold prices rose, reflecting the yen's fall. But further gains were offset by weaker spot gold prices," a trading house trader said.
The dollar rose nearly half a yen in mid-morning Tokyo to 108.15 yen after the release of the "tankan" report suggesting a worsening business outlook in Japan.
Bullion was quoted at $388.60/90 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $388.80/389.20 in New York on Tuesday.
In the gold futures market, private investors are holding massive amounts of long positions, which made investors wary of taking new positions, the traders said.
Traders here expected spot gold to be confined to narrow ranges before the expiry of OTC options in New York later today.
Platinum and palladium prices were slightly firmer on the heels of gold.
Platinum futures ranged from five to seven yen per gram higher. Newly listed benchmark August ended at 1,377 yen after opening at 1,375 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from unchanged to two yen per gram up. Newly listed benchmark August finished flat at 439 yen.
Silver futures were mostly firmer except the December contract, which fell by 0.5 yen per 10 grams. Newly listed benchmark August ended at 185.2 yen after opening at 184.0 yen.
